patches_submitted.subject: [RFC PATCH] btrfs: trigger cow fixup via dirty_folio()

version_history.subject: [RFC PATCH] btrfs: trigger cow fixup via dirty_folio()

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch proposes a new approach to trigger the COW (Copy-On-Write) fixup in Btrfs via the dirty_folio() function, which is used to handle folios that have been improperly dirtied during writeback. The current implementation uses an asynchronous worker to catch and fix such cases, but this patch aims to simplify the process by leveraging the dirty_folio() function. This change addresses a long-standing issue where a dio read may skip dirtying a folio if it is already clean by the end of the I/O operation, leading to potential data corruption. The patch maintains three critical invariants to ensure that each block is written exactly once: any dirty block is covered by delalloc or an ordered extent, any dirty block submitted into an OE will be written back within that OE, and any dirty block already submitted into an OE will not be resubmitted. This change aims to demonstrate a more complex solution to the problem and highlight the issues it must address.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary: Qu Wenruo expressed concerns that the assumption in btrfs_folio_lock() about the relationship between dirty folios and ordered extents is incorrect, potentially causing false alerts when ->dirty_folio() callback is triggered for properly dirtied blocks. He suggested simplifying the check to just verify if the fixup bit is not set.

review_comments.author: Boris Burkov (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that the delalloc lookup in btrfs_folio_cancel_fixup() can be simplified by checking if the fixup bit is not set, and agreed to rework it; also agreed to remove redundant comments and commit messages.

I think this approach here seems correct to me, except for maybe a
really mean case which calls aops->dirty_folio() without locking the folio
(not the case for dio read at least).

Won't any real reservation will cancel the fixup bits under the lock, so
the way this implementation tries to handle it is to reserve the whole
range then free the parts that don't end up getting in the "funded"
bitmap (also a bad LLM name...). This is checking the fixup bitmap under
the lock, so should see correct cancellations. Do you see an obvious
problem with that strategy, besides that it is kind of ugly and annoying
to handle the 'out:' path. Which feels similarly painful to a lot of our
other delalloc/qgroup_rsv unwinding logic with data_reserveds on OE error
or whatnot.

I think the clearer option of "take the lock, observe the real set,
release, then reserve, then take the lock and do all the work" sounds
appealing but almost certainly fails to some simple TOCTOU race.

review_comments.summary: The author acknowledged that Qu Wenruo's suggestions for simplifying the code are valid and agreed to rework the patch to address these issues. Specifically, they accepted Qu's proposal to merge canceling fixup into btrfs_folio*_set_dirty(), simplify the check for the fixup bit in EXTENT_DELALLOC, and use a helper function instead of btrfs_is_subpage() and related functions.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested splitting the set/clear of the folio fixup flag into data and metadata specific functions to avoid exposing btrfs_is_subpage() checks, and proposed implementing btrfs_folio_set_fixup() and btrfs_folio_clear_fixup() helpers. They also recommended integrating fixup cancelling into the btrfs_folio_set_dirty() helper in a future cleanup/refactor series.
review_comments.raw_body:
\u5728 2026/7/27 13:27, Boris Burkov \u5199\u9053:
[...]
>> Shouldn't we also check if we have cleared the last fixup bit and clear the
>> folio fixup flag?
>> [...]
>>> +void btrfs_folio_cancel_fixup(const struct btrfs_fs_info *fs_info,
>>> +			      struct folio *folio, u64 start, u32 len)
>>
>> Why not let IMPLEMNT_BTRFS_PAGE_OPS() to implement all the fixup helpers?
>>
> 
> I think the level 0 answer is it doesn't apply to metadata and the llm
> also went nuts messing with the macros when it tried to use them.

Right, metadata doesn't need such fixup handling at all, thus we will 
need to split the set/clear into (data|meta)_(set|clear)_func(), which 
is a little overkilled for a hot fix.

Although it would still be good to implement something like 
btrfs_folio_set_fixup() and btrfs_folio_clear_fixup(), so that we do not 
need to expose btrfs_is_subpage() checks.

And we can integrate the fixup cancelling into btrfs_folio_set_dirty() 
helper later, in a dedicated cleanup/refactor series.

Thanks,
Qu
